title: batchMint lacks nonReentrant; ERC1155 onERC1155Received fires mid-loop
description: batchMint has no nonReentrant guard. nftMinter.mint (loop body, lines 207-209) mints an ERC1155 to a caller-controlled recipient (line 188), invoking onERC1155Received mid-loop while the max payment-token approval (line 205) is live and before the nudge payout. code-scanner judged it NOT independently exploitable: the nudge reads live balanceOf at line 220 (no stale double-pay), and the dangling max approval is held by the trusted minter (address(nftMinter)), not the attacker. The residual concern is that the snapshot remaining = balanceOf at line 228 can be misattributed across nested same-token calls (cross-caller fund misattribution bounded to participating callers' own deposits in a single tx).
impact: No demonstrated cross-party value extraction. Defense-in-depth / robustness gap: under self-induced same-token reentry the balanceOf-based refund accounting (line 228) can over-/under-refund within the nested callers' own deposits. Does not touch the nudge pot or third-party funds.
attackPath: During nftMinter.mint the ERC1155 receiver hook re-enters batchMint mid-loop.

Re-entry pulls payment from the (same) msg.sender for additional real, paid mints -- attacker spends own funds; no double-nudge (balanceOf re-read live) and no drainable approval (held by trusted minter).
recommendation: Add OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard (already an expected dependency per the submodule CLAUDE.md) and mark batchMint nonReentrant, as defense-in-depth and to make the totalPaid/refund accounting robust against nested re-entry.
